gaps: The split was incomplete: the older combined draft still owned the same catalog work with divergent scope and a four-kind descriptor list, giving an implementer two competing requirement sources.
The proposed mechanism was prompt rendering only, while decision 0158 requires the model's actual tool-discovery path, so the criterion could pass while tool search still hid the dispatcher.
The claimed five runtime binding kinds do not exist: the implementation union carries a rejected legacy member and no skill_action, which belongs to a different union entirely.
An MCP pattern is not directly callable: the agent must call the proxy tool with a connected server name, so a pattern alone is neither a reachable identity nor an invocation shape.
A fixed character ceiling and 'every grant always renders' cannot both hold for an unbounded grant set.

The descriptor safety rule was underspecified and unsafe as written: local-CLI patterns derive verbatim from template remainders that may contain static operands, while the spec simultaneously forbade paths.
The replay and the live check did not falsify the real incident: a stub fed hand-built text proves the stub, and the live query filtered only two tool families.
contradictions: The spec forbade paths in descriptors while requiring reviewed argument patterns that are derived verbatim from templates which may contain them.
resolutions: The older draft now carries a superseded-in-part banner naming the confirmed capability spec as the owner of that work, and survives only as the draft source for the document contract.

The spec now pins the provider's real tool projection: the tool a descriptor names is asserted present in what the production path builds for a scheduled run, including with tool search active. Verified separately that the dispatcher is not removed from autonomous surfaces and that the failing run's own fourth attempt succeeded through it.

Corrected after reading both unions: four usable implementation kinds plus a legacy member kept only so old rows fail validation, with skill actions represented as a tool rule distinguished by source and governed by decision 0129. My earlier five-kind claim came from trusting a prior read rather than checking, and is withdrawn.
The MCP-pattern descriptor now names the proxy tool the agent actually calls together with the connected server name.

The ceiling is now derived as at least the compact representation of the granted set, so the two rules cannot conflict for any grant set, and the criterion asserts a grant set large enough to exceed any fixed value.

Owner ruled, having been shown the tradeoff twice: reviewed argument shapes render exactly as reviewed. The spec records the accepted reasoning, that these operands already appear on the approval card a human reviewed and are not credentials, and pins that no executable path, hash or credential is rendered.

The replay now builds its materialization through the production path and asserts the dispatcher is present in it before replaying, with a negative control; the live check verifies the job exists and counts every failed tool call before first success rather than two families.
open_items: The document edit contract, decisions 0108 and 0114, and the redaction sink inventory remain in the superseded draft awaiting their own spec.
Owner ruled: the live five-run check is retained evidence on the story, not a merge gate, because a live model run is not reproducible.
